title: Storage Terraform module: encryption standards, snapshot lifecycle, and migration plan for VPC/private deployments
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a single Terraform module that provides opinionated, secure defaults for EBS, EFS, and S3 used in Private (VPC) deployments. The module should enforce encryption at rest (customer-managed KMS by default), enable snapshot lifecycle policies with sane retention and backfill/migration helpers for unencrypted legacy resources, and expose configuration toggles for advanced use cases. It should include policy checks, automated tests, docs, and a staged rollout/migration plan suitable for Dedicated and Private customers.
background: Multiple private deployment customers and internal pockets of infra have differing encryption settings. Some clusters still use AWS-managed keys or have no automated snapshot lifecycle. Past incidents highlighted the compliance risk and restore complexity for unencrypted snapshots. We need an IaC-first solution with a clear migration path to avoid disruptive manual work during upgrades and to satisfy auditing demands.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module supports EBS, EFS, and S3 with encryption enabled by default
Module defaults to customer-managed KMS (configurable to service-managed) and documents KMS key policy recommendations
Snapshot lifecycle policies created for EBS/EFS and S3 lifecycle rules for point-in-time backups with configurable retention
Migration tooling or documented safe import strategy for converting existing unencrypted resources to encrypted equivalents with minimal downtime
Automated unit and integration tests (terratest/terraform-compliance) exist and run in CI
Policy checks (OPA/Conftest or Sentinel) prevent PRs that disable encryption for production workspaces
Module has example usage under examples/ for private deployment topology and is published to the internal module registry
Runbook for rollback and disaster recovery documented and reviewed by SRE and Security
tasks: Design module API: variables, outputs, defaults, and variable validation
Implement core module with resource abstractions for EBS volumes, EFS file systems, and S3 buckets
Integrate KMS key creation/binding option and support external_kms_key_id input
Add snapshot lifecycle resources: aws_backup_plan or aws_ebs_snapshot_lifecycle + lifecycle rules for S3
Implement import/migration helpers and a documented sequence for safe cutover
Add policy checks (OPA/Conftest) and CI gating
Write terratest integration tests and terraform-compliance rules
Add examples, README, upgrade notes, and runbook
Create a GitHub PR and follow internal review process; include security review checklist
implementation_notes: Prefer composing provider-agnostic interfaces where possible but use AWS primitives for the initial iteration. Use aws_kms_key with key rotation enabled for the default path. For snapshots, use AWS Backup plan for centralized retention if customer's AWS accounts allow; otherwise fall back to lifecycle rules + scheduled Lambda to enforce retention. Keep module variable surface small: enable_kms(bool), kms_key_id(string), retention_days(number), retention_archive_days(number), create_backup_plan(bool), enforce_strict_encryption(bool). When altering existing resources, do NOT allow in-place encryption changes; create new encrypted resource and orchestrate data migration followed by DNS/attachment switch in controlled window.
migration_plan: Inventory existing EBS/EFS/S3 resources across accounts using a discovery script (AWS Resource Inventory)
Flag unencrypted volumes/buckets and group by low/high-risk apps
For low-risk: snapshot/copy to encrypted volume/bucket using aws-cli or batch workers, attach/redirect, then deprecate old resources
For high-risk: plan maintenance window; use block-level replication or application-aware sync to avoid data loss
Provide an 'import' flag to module that helps import new resource IDs into Terraform state post-cutover
Automate verification checks (checksum, file counts, metadata) before final switchover
test_plan: Unit: fmt/lint/validate for all Terraform files
Integration: terratest scenario that provisions module into a throwaway VPC, runs backup lifecycle checks, and verifies encryption settings
Policy: conftest/OPA rules enforced in PR checks rejecting non-encrypted storage in production workspaces
Migration tests: run migration script in a sandbox account to validate cutover steps
E2E: sample app attaches encrypted EBS and writes/reads data across restart
rollout_plan: Merge module to main and publish versioned release to internal registry
Deploy module as default in a staging Private deployment and run smoke tests
Onboard 1 pilot internal team with non-critical workloads for 2 weeks
After pilot, run migration windows for customers using automated scripts with SRE oversight
Enforce new module defaults via CI checks and Deprecation policy for older module variants
risks: Importing existing state may be error-prone and require manual verification
Cross-account KMS ownership issues can block automated key creation
Long-running migrations for large datasets could impact availability if not properly staged
Regression in autoscaling or mount/attachment logic if module changes are not fully tested
